chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya and al-Saffar, both, from al-Ubaydi, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: A man struck a slave boy with a blow and severed part of his tongue, so he articulated some letters but not others. He said: He reads the 'Mujam' (the numerical table of letters); whatever he articulated is deducted from the blood money, and whatever he did not articulate is charged to the blood money.

I said: How is it? He said: According to the calculation of the Mujam: Alif has a diyah of one, Ba of two, Jim of three, Dal of four, Ha of five, Waw of six, Zay of seven, Ha of eight, Ta of nine, Ya of ten, Kaf of twenty, Lam of thirty, Mim of forty, Nun of fifty, Sin of sixty, Ain of seventy, Fa of eighty, Sad of ninety, Qaf of one hundred, Ra of two hundred, Shin of three hundred, Ta of four hundred, and every letter added after this from the letters of Abatath has a value of one hundred dirhams.

Whatever this report contains regarding the detailed diyah of the letters, it is permissible that it is from the speech of some of the narrators, in that they heard him say 'that is distributed among the letters of the Mujam,' so they assumed it was according to the familiar numerical calculation of those letters, and the intention was not that. Rather, the meaning was that it is divided among all the letters in equal parts, each letter being a portion of the total, as al-Sikuni detailed in his narration and others.

And if the matter were according to what this narration contains, the letters would not complete the full diyah, because that amount does not reach the complete diyah if calculated in dirhams, and if calculated in dinars, the diyah would double, and all of that is invalid. Therefore, it is appropriate that practice follows the previously mentioned reports, God willing.

key_terms.السِّكُّونِيُّ: Al-Sikuni, a specific narrator known for this interpretation

key_terms.دِيَة: Blood money or compensation for injury/death

ai.seo_question: How is blood money calculated for partial loss of tongue articulation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* details the jurisprudential debate regarding *diyah* for partial tongue severance, contrasting the literal application of *Mujam al-Huruf* (numerical letter values) with the principle of equal division (*al-qismah al-sawiyya*). Al-Tusi highlights that the numerical method is likely a misinterpretation by early narrators, as it fails to yield the complete *diyah* amount, thereby establishing the equal division method as the operative legal ruling in Shia tradition.
